videos.title: Finding a report
videos.intro: Every report in Fidato PMS is a few clicks away. In this video you will find a report, star the ones you use, and search for one that is not in your menu.

scenes.say: In the Front office menu, the part called Reports lists three screens.
Night audit is the screen that closes the day. It is not a report: it has its own chapter.
All reports holds every report your role may open.
Manager report is the one most opened, so it is in the menu itself.
All reports puts them in four groups: The day, Money owed, Statutory, and Store and equipment.
To find one, type part of its name, or a word from its description.
Click Open on a card to read the report.
Tap the star to keep a report at the top.
Your starred reports then sit under Starred, above the groups.
Tap a filled star again to take it off. Stars are kept in this browser only.
A report not in your menu is one search away. Press Control K, or click Find a screen, and type a word, such as G S T.
Not in your menu only means it is not listed for you. You may open it: click it, or press Enter.

videos.outro: That is where the reports are. The next video shows what every report has in common.

videos.title: Every report works the same way
videos.intro: Every report is laid out like a printed page, and works the same way. Here is what to look for.

scenes.say: Print prints the report alone, without the menu or the buttons.
PDF saves it as a file, made on the server from the same figures.
Excel saves a real Excel workbook.
And CSV saves a plain file that any spreadsheet opens. The buttons wait until the report has loaded.
Under the hotel's name, one line of facts says which day, or which period, the report covers.
Each report is for the hotel's business date, or its month, or its year. There is no date to choose.
A report with nothing in it still prints, and says so in words.
At the foot, Printed says when this copy was made.
And this is who made it.
A figure in red is below zero. It is real, not a mistake.
A dash is not a zero. It means the system does not hold that figure, and the notes under the report say which.

videos.outro: Until the night audit has run, today's figures can still change. A report opened at noon is the day so far.

videos.title: The Manager report
videos.intro: The Manager report is the day in three columns. It is the one an owner opens first.

scenes.say: Open Manager report in the menu. It is read afresh every time it opens.
Every line has three figures. Today. Then P T D, the period to date, from the 1st of this month. And Y T D, the year to date, from 1 April.
The facts line shows the date, where each column starts, and the currency.
The report runs in bands: room charges, extra charges, tax, revenue, payment, the ledgers, and more.
In the room summary, Sold Room counts the rooms sold. A complimentary room counts as sold.
Occupancy is the rooms sold, as a share of the rooms that could be sold.
The average daily rate is the room charges divided by the rooms sold. Extras, food and tax are not in it.
Revenue per available room divides the room charges by every room that could be sold. It falls when rooms stay empty.
Below the statistics, the POS summary is the restaurant, outlet by outlet.

videos.outro: A complimentary room lifts the occupancy and lowers the average rate, because it earns nothing.

videos.title: The Night audit report
videos.intro: The Night audit report is one day, to the paisa. It only reads the day: the night audit itself is run on its own screen.

scenes.say: Open All reports, then Night audit report. It is wider than the screen, so it scrolls sideways. Here it is drawn smaller, to show every column.
Room Charges lists every room charged for the night: the booking, the guest, where the booking came from, and the rate.
Var % is how far the rate given is below the room's normal rate.
Checkin By names who checked the guest in. A dash means it was not recorded.
Complimentary lists the rooms given free.
Checked Out is who left today, with their bill. A balance below zero means the guest paid more than the bill came to.
Daily Sales shows the day's sales by type, with their tax.
Receipt Detail lists every payment taken, by method.
Then the receipts by user.
And by payment method.
Room Status counts the rooms: occupied, due out, vacant, departed, reserved and blocked. Occupied means checked in.
Pax Status counts the guests who arrived, checked out, and stayed over.
Pax Analysis splits the guests by rate type.
And the POS summary is the restaurant's day.

videos.outro: Before the audit runs, a guest who has not arrived is still in Room Charges. They go when the night audit marks the no-show.

videos.title: Occupancy and statistics
videos.intro: Three reports show the month and the year: Monthly occupancy, Monthly statistics, and Yearly statistics.

scenes.say: Monthly occupancy covers the business date's month.
One bar per day shows the occupancy, in percent. Full houses and empty days both stand out.
Monthly statistics is the same month as a grid, one row per day.
Night Sold is the rooms sold that night.
Next to it, the occupancy. Complimentary rooms count with the rooms sold.
Then the average daily rate, and the revenue per available room.
Expense is not recorded in this system, so it is a dash, never a zero.
Days after today have figures too: the nights already booked, at the booking's rate. They change if the booking changes.
Yearly statistics has the same columns, one row per month from January to December, with a grand total for the year.

videos.outro: Rooms are counted from the day the hotel first traded. Earlier days show nothing.

videos.title: Money owed
videos.intro: Four reports show money still owed, and money taken: City ledger, No show, Guest ledger and Cashier shift.

scenes.say: City ledger is the bills sent to a company or a booking site, account by account, for the business date.
Ignore zero balance account is on when it opens. Turn it off to see every account, even those with nothing on them.
The facts line says the day, and whether zero balances are left out.
Each account shows its opening balance, the bills sent to it, what it paid, and its closing balance.
No show lists the bookings that never arrived on the day. When everybody came, it still prints, and says so.
Guest ledger is every guest's bill that moved from the 1st of the month to the business date: opening, charges, received and closing.
A closing in red is below zero: more was received than charged.
This report has Print and CSV only.
Cashier shift is what each cashier took on the business date, by method.
Not on record means the payment was taken before the system recorded who took it. Nobody's name is guessed.
Each method is its own row, with how many receipts and how much.
A receipt that was reversed is not money the cashier holds, so it is left out.

videos.outro: The revenue manager does not see City ledger, Guest ledger or Cashier shift.

videos.title: The statutory reports
videos.intro: Three reports are for filing with the government: Lodging tax, the GST sales register, and the Form 3 register. This system files nothing itself.

scenes.say: Lodging tax covers the whole month.
Check Out Bills has one row for each day a bill was issued, with that day's first and last bill number.
CGST and SGST are each half the tax the bills carried, on the room rent less its discount.
Bill numbers run on with no gap. A gap is an audit finding.
The group's accountant confirms this sheet before anything is filed from it.
The GST sales register lists every invoice and credit note issued this month, as the GST return wants them.
The total line counts the documents.
A credit note is its own row, below zero. The place of supply is always the hotel's own state.
CSV saves the columns the GST return upload wants.
The Form 3 register lists the foreign guests who arrived this month, and how many still await an FRRO number.
This system does not file with the FRRO. Filing happens on the government portal.
The portal's numbers are typed on the Form 3 screen, and show here.

videos.outro: The Form 3 register shows passports, so only the people who check guests in can open it.

videos.title: The accounting export
videos.intro: The Accounting export hands your accountant the hotel's days as a file. It reads the same figures the reports print, and changes nothing.

scenes.say: Open it with Find a screen: type tally, or export. It is for the owner, an admin, the GM and the accountant.
From starts on the 1st of the month. This day is included.
To is the business date. This day is included too.
Choose the day book, as a CSV or as an Excel file: one row a day.
The two Tally choices make no file yet. They wait for the ledger names in your own books.
Check the table below, then tap Export.
If the night audit has not run for some of the days, a yellow note says so. Their figures may still change.
The Night audit column says Closed, or Not run, for each day.
Received from companies is kept apart from sales and receipts.
This counts what was charged and received each day. Lodging tax counts the bills issued, so a stay still in house is here and not there.

videos.outro: Tell your accountant before you send a month that is not closed.

videos.title: The Store and equipment reports
videos.intro: Nine reports show what the stores hold and use, and where the equipment is.

scenes.say: On the Store, tap Reports.
Choose a report. Closing stock is the first of the nine.
Or find Store reports with Find a screen: all nine on one page.
Click Open on a card.
They cover closing stock, movement by day, consumption, wastage and breakage, count differences, dead stock, days of cover, supplier spend, and the equipment.
Closing stock is as on the business date.
Each store lists its items: on hand, the unit cost, and the value, as recorded.
Then the store's total.
All stores sums up every store.

videos.outro: Costs are as recorded: delivery prices before GST, at the running average. A price nobody recorded is a dash.

videos.title: Which report answers which question
videos.intro: Here is which report answers which question.
checklist: How did today go? The Manager report.
One whole day, to the paisa? The Night audit report.
How full were we? Monthly occupancy, or Monthly statistics.
What do companies owe? City ledger.
Who did not come? No show.
What did each cashier take? Cashier shift.
The month's tax? Lodging tax, and the GST sales register.
Foreign guests filed? The Form 3 register.
The month for the accountant? Accounting export.
What is in the stores? Closing stock.
videos.outro: That is the reports. Thank you for watching.
